rules.text: If the query image displays a distinct, focal hyperintense (bright) lesion or mass that is clearly absent in the provided normal reference images, trust A (Agent).
If the query image shows standard anatomical structures (e.g., ventricles, sulci) that appear symmetrical and intact, matching the general appearance of the normal reference images, trust B (Direct).
If Branch A identifies an anomaly based on 'enlarged ventricles' or 'structural deviation' but the ventricles appear symmetrical and within normal limits compared to the references, trust B (Direct).
The brain tissue is centrally located within the image frame, surrounded by a black background.
The brain cross-section exhibits a continuous, roughly oval or circular outer boundary.
The image consists of a grayscale palette (black background, gray/white tissue) with no other colors.
The brain tissue displays a granular, heterogeneous texture with visible internal structures.
Do not flag mild asymmetry in lateral ventricle size or shape as a tumor anomaly.
Ignore subtle periventricular hyperintensities or signal variations that lack distinct mass effect or borders.
Do not classify global image blurriness, noise, or low contrast as structural brain anomalies.
